---------------------------------------------------------------- Surfaces
Two layers of neutrals: the content is the lightest surface (in light
mode) or the highest one (in dark), while chrome and panels recede. A
slightly warm cast — paper, not screen.
1. The service worker first: it alone can write back into the caches.

Light / dark theme.
*
Rendering does not depend on this module: `tokens.css` already follows the
system via `light-dark()`, so the page is painted correctly before React
even starts. This module exists only to *force* a theme, by setting
`data-theme` on <html>, which redefines `color-scheme` and nothing else.
does not loop on a corrupted tree

Nook's design tokens.

One place defines a value. The colours use `light-dark()`: the light value
and the dark value live side by side, and `color-scheme` decides. One
important consequence: the theme follows the system from the first pixel
painted, with no JavaScript.

That is a constraint, not a preference — the product's CSP forbids inline
scripts, so the usual trick of a small anti-flash script in the <head> is
impossible here. Switching manually is done by setting `data-theme` on
<html>, which does nothing but redefine `color-scheme`.
Two encryptions of the same text must be indistinguishable from one
